title: AI Agent Company Decagon Has Held Early M&A Talks and Hired a Banker
key_facts: Decagon, an AI agent start-up last valued at $4.5 billion earlier this year, has hired a bank to evaluate acquisition interest, according to people familiar with the matter.
It held early talks with ServiceNow; a ServiceNow spokesperson says they are not ongoing (the story was updated to say so).
Early talks with other companies also took place; if no deal materialises Decagon could raise a new funding round instead.
ServiceNow's Amit Zavery, president and chief product officer: "Our approach to M&A has not changed: we remain an organic growth company first."
Decagon, founded in July 2023 by Jesse Zhang and Ashwin Sreenivas, uses generative AI to automate customer support for Delta, Snapchat and Ticketmaster, among others; it has raised over $400 million.
It competes with Sierra, led by Bret Taylor and valued at $15.8 billion earlier this year.
Business Insider links the interest to a shift in the AI boom, with tech companies buying their way into AI markets, citing Nvidia's purchase of Hugging Face and Stripe's purchase of OpenRouter.
quote_evidence: The company, which was last valued at $4.5 billion earlier this year, has hired a bank to evaluate acquisition interest, according to people familiar with the matter.
Decagon held early discussions with cloud software giant ServiceNow, but a spokesperson for ServiceNow says they're not ongoing.

why_it_matters_hint: A sale of a leading AI customer-support agent company would be another sign of big firms buying into AI markets.
event_date: Reported 13 Oct 2026 (late); article updated after ServiceNow's comment
notes: Anonymous sources; ServiceNow says its talks are not ongoing. Dollar amounts for the Hugging Face and OpenRouter deals appear in the article but are not used.
